title: Sign language basics
examples: Is sign language just like talking?
Do I need to learn different signs for different countries?
How do I spell words with my hands?

explain.say: Today we are learning that signs are actually full languages.
Some sign languages are different from others.
We can learn to spell words using our fingers.
Learning signs helps us communicate with everyone.
When we use signs, we are using a whole language system.
A real life example is watching a sign language interpreter.

faq.q: Is sign language the same everywhere?
faq.a: No, sign languages are different depending on the country or region. For example, British Sign Language is not the same as American Sign Language.
asks: Are all sign languages the same?
Do I need to learn different signs?

faq.q: How do I learn the signs?
faq.a: The best way is to practice with native signers and use dedicated learning resources. Consistency is very important when learning any language.
asks: Is there an app for this?
What is the best way to start?

faq.q: What is the difference between signing and just pointing?
faq.a: Pointing is just showing where something is. Signing uses specific hand shapes and movements that have meaning in the language.
asks: What makes a sign a sign?
Can I just use my hands?

faq.q: Do I need to learn the alphabet for every country?
faq.a: You only need to learn the fingerspelling alphabet for the specific sign language you are studying. Each language has its own unique set of signs.
asks: Do I learn the alphabet for every language?
How many letters do I need to learn?

faq.q: Is sign language just for deaf people?
faq.a: No, sign language is a tool for communication that many people use. It helps connect people regardless of hearing ability.
asks: Is it only for the hearing impaired?
Is it a language for everyone?

facts: Sign languages are complete languages with their own grammar and syntax.
BSL and ASL are distinct languages, not just different ways of signing the same things.
Fingerspelling uses a manual alphabet to represent letters of the written word.
The specific signs and grammar change between different regions.

quiz.say: If you learn American Sign Language, can you use those signs in Britain?
quiz.why: Because ASL and BSL are separate languages with different signs and grammar.

wrong.0: This is tempting because some basic signs might look similar, but the grammar is different.
wrong.1: This is tempting because people are individuals, but the language rules are fixed.
wrong.3: This is tempting because they both use hands, but they are different languages.

quiz.say: What is the main purpose of fingerspelling?

options.show: To show the order of things
options.say: To show the order of things

options.show: To represent letters of a word
options.say: To represent letters of a word

quiz.why: Fingerspelling helps you communicate words that do not have a single sign.

wrong.0: Order is usually shown by sequence or time, not the alphabet.
wrong.1: Greetings use specific signs, not the letters of the alphabet.
wrong.3: Counting is usually done with numbers, not the alphabet.

quiz.say: If a sign language is a language, what must it have?
quiz.why: All languages, spoken or signed, follow grammatical rules to make sense.

wrong.1: Having many signs is good, but it does not make it a language.
wrong.2: A dictionary lists words, but it does not explain how to put them together.
wrong.3: While culture influences it, grammar is the defining feature of a language.
